extracted.intended_audience: educators, curriculum designers, policymakers, after-school program leaders, media literacy researchers, and parents interested in media education and participatory culture
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing media-education programs that prepare young people for participatory culture by developing cultural competencies, social skills, and ethical frameworks across school and informal learning contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Participatory Culture
rubrics_metrics.description: A participatory culture is a culture with relatively low barriers to artistic expression and civic engagement; strong support for creating and sharing creations; some type of informal mentorship whereby experienced participants pass along knowledge to novices; members who believe their contributions matter; and members who feel some degree of social connection with one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every member must contribute, but all must believe they are free to contribute and that what they contribute will be appropriately valued. Emphasize cultural/institutional supports, not just technical affordances, when assessing or designing participatory environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliations (form of participatory culture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Memberships, formal and informal, in online communities centered around various forms of media (e.g., Friendster, Facebook, MySpace, message boards, metagaming, game clans).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how a setting supports community belonging, shared norms, and repeated interaction across members; look for evidence of membership structures and pathways for newcomers to engage and advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressions (form of participatory culture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Producing new creative forms such as digital sampling, skinning and modding, fan videos, fan fiction, zines, or mash-ups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess opportunities and supports for creative production, tools provided or accessible, and norms around sharing, remixing, and attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative problem solving (form of participatory culture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Working together in teams, formal and informal, to complete tasks and develop new knowledge, such as through Wikipedia, alternative reality gaming, or 'spoiling'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure whether environments enable distributed tasking, coordination, peer feedback, and shared goals; look for scaffolds for collaboration and mechanisms for synthesizing contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circulations (form of participatory culture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shaping the flow of media, such as podcasting or blogging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how participants can disseminate, reframe, and redistribute content; evaluate platforms' affordances for reach, commenting, and remix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play (new media literacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The capacity to experiment with the surroundings as a form of problem solving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster environments that encourage trial-and-error, low-cost experimentation, and safe failure; avoid overly prescriptive tasks that block exploratory problem solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance (new media literacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to adopt alternative identities for the purpose of improvisation and discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support role-play, avatar use, and persona experimentation as legitimate learning modes; recognize performance as a way to rehearse and reflect on different viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulation (new media literacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to interpret and construct dynamic models of real-world processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate simulation tools and teach students to read and build models; evaluate understanding of model assumptions and limits as part of assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation (new media literacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to meaningfully sample and remix media content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach sampling/remix practices alongside discussions of intellectual property and attribution; assess meaningfulness of remixes (not just technical assembly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multitasking (new media literacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to scan the environment and shift focus onto salient details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish productive multitasking (monitoring multiple streams for relevant cues) from distractive behavior; design tasks that require rapid attention shifts to valued goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributed cognition (new media literacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to interact meaningfully with tools that expand mental capacities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how learners use external tools (software, devices, shared artifacts) to think with and whether they can integrate tool-supported reasoning into their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective intelligence (new media literacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to pool knowledge and compare notes with others toward a common goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate participation in knowledge-building practices (e.g., wiki contributions, crowd-sourced problem solving) and the capacity to synthesize diverse inputs into coherent outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgment (new media literacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to evaluate the reliability and credibility of different information sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach critical evaluation heuristics, source triangulation, and contextual assessment; assess learners' evidence-based reasoning and ability to distinguish authoritative from suspect sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmedia navigation (new media literacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to follow the flow of stories and information across multiple modalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess learners' ability to locate, link, and interpret information that is distributed across platforms and formats, and to reconstruct narratives or arguments from such fragments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Networking (new media literacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to search for, synthesize, and disseminate information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure skills in locating peers and resources, building connections, curating content, and broadcasting responsibly to relevant audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiation (new media literacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to travel across diverse communities, discerning and respecting multiple perspectives, and grasping and following alternative norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include assessments of intercultural communication, norm translation, conflict resolution, and ethical engagement across communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Participation Gap (core problem to address)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unequal access to the opportunities, experiences, skills, and knowledge that prepare youths for full participation in the new media world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and pedagogy should move beyond simple hardware access to provide supported opportunities, sustained connectivity, storage/transmission capacity, and instructional resources; avoid treating access as sufficient without training and contextual supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Transparency Problem (core problem to address)
rubrics_metrics.description: The challenge that young people may not recognize how media shape perceptions of the world and therefore cannot fully articulate what they learn from participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design curricula that make media processes explicit, scaffold reflection, and teach students to analyze how media construction affects meaning and audience reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Ethics Challenge (core problem to address)
rubrics_metrics.description: The breakdown of traditional forms of professional training and socialization that would prepare young people for public roles as media makers and community participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit instruction and guided practice in ethical norms, attribution, privacy, and civic responsibility; avoid leaving ethical development entirely to informal peer cultures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affinity Spaces as Learning Environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal, peer-based learning communities sustained by common endeavors that bridge age, class, race, gender, and educational differences, allow varied participation according to skill and interest, depend on peer-to-peer teaching, and let participants feel like experts while tapping others' expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing or evaluating programs, value participation diversity, distributed mentorship (beta-reading, peer feedback), opportunities to play expert roles, and mechanisms for peer teaching and scaffolding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ecological Approach to Media Education
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on the interrelationship among communication technologies, the cultural communities that grow up around them, and the activities they support, rather than treating technologies in isolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess programs by how well they integrate tools, cultural practices, legal/political/economic contexts, and social institutions; avoid narrow technology-centric interventions that ignore cultural supports and practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systemic Approach to Media Education (who should respond)
rubrics_metrics.description: Everyone involved—schools, after-school programs, parents, and community institutions—has distinctive roles in encouraging and nurturing the skills necessary for becoming full participants in society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design coordinated interventions across formal and informal settings, clarifying responsibilities and leveraging complementary strengths (e.g., schools for fundamentals, after-school for production projects, parents for supervision and values).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift focus from access to participation/opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Move the digital-divide discourse from questions of technological access to opportunities for participation and development of cultural competencies and social skills needed for full involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate equity not only by device/connectivity distribution but by availability of meaningful participation opportunities, mentorship, and practices that build literacies; avoid metrics that count hardware without measuring participation or learning outcomes.
